preconditions.description: The number of queries q must be between 1 and 10,000.
Each query must have an integer n representing the length of the permutation, which must be between 1 and 100.
Each query must have an integer k representing the desired beauty, which must be between 1 and the maximum possible beauty for a permutation of length n.

postconditions.description: If a valid permutation exists, output 'YES' followed by the permutation; otherwise, output 'NO'.

postconditions.expression: any((i in range(1, n + 1) for i in stdout.split()[1:]))
postconditions.description: The output permutation must contain all integers from 1 to n exactly once.

postconditions.expression: sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) for j in range(i, n + 1) if set(range(i, j + 1)).issubset(set(map(int, stdout.split()[1:])))) == k
postconditions.description: The beauty of the output permutation must equal k, counting all valid consecutive segments.
